comparison: Perfect agreement on ocular dominance mapping findings (C32-C38). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval emphasizing the technical evidence from Figure 1B-C and appropriate literature contextualization, while peer reviewers note consistency with established knowledge and praise the novel spatial resolution achievement.

Complete agreement on monocular response patterns (C5, C39-C41, C44). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the visual clarity of ODI-dependent patterns but mentions lack of explicit p-values, while peer reviewers accept findings as expected and consistent with ocular dominance principles.

Strong agreement on binocular response findings (C6-C8, C42, C45-C46). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the flattened binocular response functions and statistical evidence (p<0.001), while peer reviewers highlight this as the key surprising finding showing ODI-dependent suppression/enhancement. Peer review also includes C9, C47-C49 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both address statistical evidence for ODI-dependent binocular modulation (C47-C49). OpenEval provides SUPPORTED evaluation focusing on the explicit p<0.001 statistical evidence and linear model appropriateness. Peer review includes these claims within broader binocular response evaluation (R4) and strongly endorses the findings.

Strong agreement on modeling work (C10, C50-C61, C79-C80). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes model fit quality (0.87-0.94) and mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers praise the large-scale simultaneous recording approach and advancement over previous work. Peer review also includes C56 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Partial overlap on binocular response levels (C9). OpenEval provides SUPPORTED evaluation for C9, C56, C63 noting qualitative description without statistical testing. Peer review includes C9 within broader binocular findings (R4) with strong endorsement of the overall pattern.

Minimal overlap on model parameters (C56). OpenEval evaluates C9, C56, C63 as SUPPORTED regarding median response levels. Peer review R5 focuses on broader modeling work (C10, C50-C61, C79-C80) with only C56 in common, which is endorsed as part of the overall modeling framework.

Minimal overlap on functional interpretation (C63). OpenEval evaluates C9, C56, C63 as SUPPORTED with note about qualitative description. Peer review R6 addresses C62-C66 interpretations and finds them SUPPORTED, with C63 included as part of accepted functional significance claims.

Divergent evaluations on functional interpretations (C62, C64-C66). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are inferences requiring additional experiments for causal claims. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretations and noting authors 'deftly contextualize these important findings.' This represents a meaningful disagreement on the strength of evidence for functional significance claims.

Agreement on discrepancies with prior work (C20-C22, C67-C71). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the large sample size strengthening contradictory findings versus Dougherty et al. 2019. Peer reviewers accept these differences and note authors appropriately contextualize findings in literature.

Agreement on methodological speculation (C72-C76). Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are reasonable but speculative explanations for discrepancies, not empirically tested. Peer reviewers acknowledge the uncertainty remains unresolved and suggest future work combining imaging with electrophysiology.

Agreement on depth and temporal limitations (C84-C87). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges these as well-established constraints of two-photon imaging. Peer reviewers explicitly note the superficial layer limitation and confirm authors appropriately address methodological limitations.

Divergent evaluations on GCaMP linearity concerns (C89-C91). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the linearity range is citation-supported and speculation is appropriately cautious. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising then dismissing concerns about calcium signal nonlinearity potentially exaggerating effects, representing acknowledged but unresolved uncertainty.

Agreement on methodology quality (C4, C26-C31). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes technical details including sample sizes, controls, and selection criteria. Peer reviewers praise the well-executed approach, large dataset, and high spatial resolution. OpenEval addresses many additional methodological claims (C92-C114) not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

OpenEval evaluated literature contextualization claims (C77-C78, C81-C83) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate characterization of prior modeling work and identification of gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these literature review claims, though peer reviewers generally praised contextualization.
